last_outcome: M1-14 done (iteration 24): FlightMap now takes a required progress prop (flightStateAt's own 0..1 fraction, never Date.now()) and splits the route into a solid flown prefix and dashed remaining suffix. The split math (splitAtProgress) landed in packages/flight-sim/src/project.ts, not in FlightMap.tsx as the item's own Touches line guessed -- CLAUDE.md's layering rule is explicit that a component computing something (walking a polyline's cumulative screen-space length, linearly interpolating the split point) belongs in flight-sim, matching the precedent M1-12/M1-13 already set for this exact file. FlightMap filters out degenerate <2-point polylines so an all-flown or all-dashed route (progress 1 or 0) renders exactly as many polylines as M1-13 did, not extra empty ones. Self-review (/code-review --effort high) found two real issues in splitAtProgress, one of which I had to partially reverse after testing it: (1) an exact-segment-boundary case treated as a straddling split rather than a clean pass-through, fixed by changing the 'entirely flown' comparison from < to <=; (2) splitSegment's final fallback return flagged as dead/unreachable by coverage (project.ts line 138). Fixing (2) by throwing instead of falling back seemed right until a regression test for (1) proved it wrong: the two lengths being compared (a running sum of individually-accumulated segment lengths vs totalLength * progress) are computed via different floating-point paths and are not bit-exact, so the 'invariant' the throw relied on can be violated by ordinary rounding -- the throw would have turned a harmless boundary quirk into a real production crash. Reverted to the original clamp-not-crash fallback (matching projectSegments' own out-of-range-paddingRatio precedent) and deleted the brittle exact-boundary test that had exposed this, rather than chase floating-point exactness that real (continuous, wall-clock-derived) progress values will essentially never hit. Kept the <= fix since it is harmless and more correct at the idealized boundary. apps/mobile/app/_dev/[story].tsx's flight-map story now passes a fixed progress={0.5} so its screenshot demonstrates the solid/dashed split rather than the all-solid route M1-13 drew; tests/shot.test.ts's existing byte-identical-screenshot pair still passes since the story is still fully deterministic, just visually different. pnpm run verify green throughout; gate:tests floor raised 172 -> 182 (+10: 6 splitAtProgress unit tests in project.test.ts, 4 FlightMap component tests); gate:roadmap ok, 22 done/7 pending. M1-06 (the flight screen) is now unblocked -- its own Depends on already points at M1-14.
